action: Port users and shippers should use only channels announced by the Autoridade Portuária de Santos and the Federal Police, and treat unexpected emails or calls about cargo, access or payments with caution.
date_note: Systems went down on 6 November; the ransom demand was reported on 17 November, which is the date used here.
exec: A major Brazilian port authority says it received a ransom demand after its systems went down on 6 November; cargo paperwork runs on workarounds.
impact: Website and internal systems down since 6 November; some services run through the federal Porto Sem Papel system. Data said to be in backups and being recovered; no ransom amount was reported.
plain: Brazil's Port of Santos authority says hackers demanded money after its systems went down on 6 November. Its website and internal systems were affected and are being restored from backups.

key_findings: Baguete (10 Nov): APS confirmed a cyberattack on port systems, down since the morning of 6 Nov; it first cited a power outage hitting its servers and had not determined scale or whether data was accessed.
Cesportos raised the port protection level to II; the Federal Police office in Santos said it had been notified but had received no documents or opened an inquiry.

O POVO (17 Nov): APS confirmed it received a ransom demand from hackers claiming the attack; preliminary investigation points to action from outside Brazil; a report is being prepared for the Federal Police.
APS says data was kept in backups and is being recovered, and believes the virus had been present since at least 6 Nov.

summary: The Santos Port Authority confirmed a cyberattack on its systems, down since 6 November. On 17 November O POVO reported the authority had received a ransom demand and that preliminary findings point to an origin outside Brazil. Its first account cited a power failure; the two reports do not fully agree on cause. The authority says data is being recovered from backups.
title: Santos port authority says it received a ransom demand after systems went down on 6 November

validation.note: The cyberattack and outage from 6 Nov are reported by both Baguete (10 Nov) and O POVO (17 Nov), but the ransom demand, origin outside Brazil and backup recovery appear only in O POVO, a general article that names no APS spokesperson. Baguete cites a power failure; O POVO gives no cause.

review.note: Compared title, dates, 6 Nov outage, ransom demand, backups, outside-Brazil origin against O POVO (17 Nov) and Baguete (10 Nov): facts match. Validation was corroborated but the ransom claim appears only in O POVO (no named spokesperson, no amount); set single_source.
